findings.passage: The two readings make different predictions from here. If Reiter is a Three, a season of applause will teach her to believe it. If she is a Six, the applause will keep feeling like something to hand to someone else.
findings.problem: The closing test counts growing comfort with praise as Type 3 evidence, but the record already shows the aversion easing, and both witnesses describe it as habituation. In the April 2026 Zavidow episode (S42 0:08:35-0:08:47) he says "like you got to get used to it" (the draft cuts this line). She answers "I feel like I'm good at it now", he says "you're getting better", and later in the episode she says she no longer thinks about turning to God (C41). Afualo's own closing line predicts that repetition alone will stop the grimace. Someone of any type, aged 25 to 30 and applauded on network TV for a season, would plausibly get used to compliments. On the article's own terms, ordinary maturation would flip the type at the next refresh. The present-tense type answer ("she pushes praise away, wishes for someone or something to hold her success") would then read as false, even though the 2025-2026 behavior it rests on stays true. C110's review trigger inherits the same confound.
findings.acceptance_test: (1) The closing no longer names learning to believe the applause as the Three outcome. Any forward-looking signal is one habituation would not produce by itself, e.g. whether new success becomes the next metric or goal versus being attributed outward to people, preparation or structure, or what she says she is protecting when she turns work down. (2) The type argument mentions the documented April 2026 easing once and says a fading discomfort with compliments would not by itself settle the type. (3) The type answer or the paragraph directly after it dates the pattern (e.g. "in 2025 and 2026"), so the central description stays true if the habit fades. (4) C110's review_trigger is rewritten to match the new signal.

findings.passage: When she can describe a hard week there at length, will she credit the response (Three), or the castmates, preparation and someone in charge who got her through it (Six)?
findings.problem: This is billed as "the clearest test", but crediting castmates, writers and the show's leadership is the standard script for any SNL cast member speaking to the press. A refresh would read routine professional humility as Six confirmation, which is the incentive comparison the standard asks for. The test is also tied to SNL ("there"), and featured players can leave after a single season, so by 2028-2031 the question may refer to a job she no longer has. C101's trigger repeats both problems.
findings.acceptance_test: The settle question (a) names a setting where the press script is weak, such as an unscripted long-form podcast or her own channel rather than network promotion. (b) It says what a Three answer and a Six answer would each sound like beyond crediting colleagues, e.g. whether she describes a low point as a threat to her standing or as fear of being found out or losing support, and what she turned to. (c) It is worded to work whether or not she is still on SNL at the next refresh, e.g. "her first hard stretch in network television". C101's review_trigger is updated to match.

assessment: Five-year test: mostly passes. With the latest events removed (SNL casting, Netflix premiere, Twilight), the thesis still stands. The hook is May 2025, and the argument rests on dated 2025-2026 self-reports plus three independent witnesses (roommate, Soresi, Afualo). SNL appears as context and as a future test, not as proof. Most changing facts are dated and carry actionable triggers (C08, C12-C15, C52, C56, C57, C60), and the podcast, parody and Twilight FAQs give absolute dates. The weak point is the forward tests. Both settle signals are confounded in ways a 2027-2031 refresh would misread: future-01 (ordinary habituation, already visible in April 2026, is counted as Three evidence) and future-02 (SNL press humility is counted as Six evidence). Fix those, and the page can be reopened without flipping on noise. Smaller items are expiring tense: the Minimum Wage FAQ is in the future tense (future-03), "now performs" and "At 25 she is" (future-04), and a yearless "mid-October" (future-05). The evidence window is stated relatively (future-06) and there are fragile links (future-07). The meta_title's "Why Praise Makes Her Uneasy" is present tense on the same behavior as future-01; if the edit dates the pattern in the body, the title can stand as the thesis. Similarity advisory: tripped at 0.053 against Shyam Sankar on the shared phrase "core emotion". That is ordinary triad vocabulary, not reuse. The Inde Navarrette pair (0.049) shares only the general "the evidence is what she does with X" move. Compared directly, the arguments differ: Navarrette walks toward fear after being cast, while Reiter pushes approval away when it arrives. No finding. The recent run of young-performer Sixes (Navarrette, Zada, Reiter) is worth watching at the corpus level, but this argument is specific to her. Verification was limited to what this role needs: I reopened the saved S42 transcript at 0:08:27-0:08:56 to confirm the easing exchange and ran an iTunes lookup for the Passion Pod episode page. I did not reopen the other sources.
